{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01ADU9zhvsJvnSognLEwobVD","type":"tool_result","content":"\"\"\"Command-line package: `main(argv) -> int` dispatches to handlers registered by command stories.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import main, register_command\nfrom cli import init_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `init` handler at import\n\n__all__ = [\"main\", \"register_command\"]\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; registering a name again replaces the handler.\"\"\"\n    _handlers[name] = handler\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Validate `argv`, dispatch `argv[0]` to its registered handler, and return the exit code.\"\"\"\n    args = list(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)\n    try:\n        usage.validate(args, _handlers)\n    except usage.UsageError as exc:\n        print(f\"error: {exc}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    handler = _handlers.get(args[0])\n    if handler is None:\n        print(f\"error: command not available in this build: {args[0]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return USAGE_ERROR\n    return handler(args[1:])\n\"\"\"The `init` command: empty the rates store, print nothing, exit 0.\n\nThe schema is provisioned by the DATABASE step, so init never runs DDL or opens a driver. It\nremoves every stored rate through the declared `rates.delete_from_date` operation, passing a date\nearlier than any publication, and leaves the table in place with no rows.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\n\nEARLIEST_DATE = \"0000-01-01\"\n\n\ndef init(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Remove every stored rate and return 0. The argument list is validated before dispatch.\"\"\"\n    db = open_store()\n    try:\n        db.rates.delete_from_date(from_date=EARLIEST_DATE)\n    finally:\n        db.close()\n    return 0\n\n\nregister_command(\"init\", init)\n\"\"\"Argument validation for the fxrates command line.\n\n`validate` runs before dispatch and rejects a malformed invocation with `UsageError`, so the caller\ncan exit 2 with empty stdout and one stderr line. It never opens a database or binds a socket.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport re\nfrom collections.abc import Collection\n\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\nPORT_FLAG = \"--port\"\nPORT_MIN = 1\nPORT_MAX = 65535\n\n# Exact positional argument counts for the commands whose stories are in the blueprint table.\n_ARITY: dict[str, int] = {\"init\": 0, \"load\": 1, \"fetch\": 0}\n_SERVE = \"serve\"\n\n\nclass UsageError(Exception):\n    \"\"\"A malformed invocation. The message is one line; its wording is not part of the contract.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef validate(argv: list[str], registered: Collection[str] = ()) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Raise UsageError unless `argv` names a known command with well-formed arguments.\n\n    `registered` holds the names of commands with a handler. A command outside the table above\n    and outside `registered` is a usage error; a registered command outside the table is not\n    arity-checked.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not argv:\n        raise UsageError(\"no command given; usage: fxrates <command> [arguments...]\")\n    command, rest = argv[0], list(argv[1:])\n    if command == _SERVE:\n        _validate_serve(rest)\n    elif command in _ARITY:\n        _validate_arity(command, rest)\n    elif command not in registered:\n        raise UsageError(f\"unknown command: {command}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_arity(command: str, rest: list[str]) -> None:\n    if rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return\n    expected = _ARITY[command]\n    if len(rest) != expected:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{command} takes {expected} argument(s), got {len(rest)}\")\n\n\ndef _validate_serve(rest: list[str]) -> None:\n    if not rest or rest == [HELP_FLAG]:\n        return\n    if len(rest) != 2 or rest[0] != PORT_FLAG:\n        raise UsageError(f\"serve takes an optional {PORT_FLAG} <n>\")\n    _validate_port(rest[1])\n\n\ndef _validate_port(value: str) -> None:\n    if not re.fullmatch(r\"[0-9]+\", value) or not PORT_MIN <= int(value) <= PORT_MAX:\n        raise UsageError(f\"{PORT_FLAG} must be an integer from {PORT_MIN} to {PORT_MAX}, got {value!r}\")\n\"\"\"In-process test helper: runs the dispatcher without spawning a process.\"\"\"\n\nimport contextlib\nimport io\n\nfrom cli import main\n\n\ndef cli_runner(*args: str) -> tuple[int, str, str]:\n    \"\"\"Return (exit_code, stdout, stderr) for the given arguments.\"\"\"\n    out, err = io.StringIO(), io.StringIO()\n    with contextlib.redirect_stdout(out), contextlib.redirect_stderr(err):\n        code = main(list(args))\n    return code, out.getvalue(), err.getvalue()\n\"\"\"Lets `python -m cli` run the dispatcher; the launcher `fxrates` uses this form.\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli import main\n\nsys.exit(main())\n----\n\"\"\"ECB history file validation: one pure function checks a whole file before any write.\n\n`parse_history` reads the text of an ECB euro reference rate history file and returns every\nnon-N/A value as (date, currency, rate_text). It performs no database access and reads no file.\nRates keep their published text; they are never converted to a number.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport re\nfrom decimal import Decimal\n\nFIRST_HEADER_FIELD = \"Date\"\nNOT_AVAILABLE = \"N/A\"\n\n_DATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}\")\n_CURRENCY_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[A-Z]{3}\")\n_RATE_PATTERN = re.compile(r\"[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?\")\n\n\nclass RejectedFile(Exception):\n    \"\"\"Raised when an ECB history file violates the format; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\"\"\"\n    if fields and fields[-1] == \"\":\n        return fields[:-1]\n    return fields\n\n\ndef _check_date(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed date: {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has an impossible date: {text!r}\") from error\n\n\ndef _check_rate(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _RATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed rate: {text!r}\")\n    if Decimal(text) == 0:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a zero rate: {text!r}\")\n\"\"\"Database location: one place decides which store the application opens.\n\nResolution order: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db. The environment is read at\ncall time. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())\n\"\"\"FxRates application package.\n\nApplication modules (config, ecb, fetch, rates, history, convert, commands) are added by later\nbuild blocks. Database access goes through the shipped `persistence` package only.\n\"\"\"\n----\n#!/bin/sh\n# fxrates — application launcher. Activates .venv when present and hands the arguments to the\n# cli package. It holds no command logic; every command is dispatched by cli.main.\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$ROOT\"\nif [ -f \"$ROOT/.venv/bin/activate\" ]; then\n    . \"$ROOT/.venv/bin/activate\"\nfi\nexec python -m cli \"$@\"\n----\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit for project tests; under the acceptance harness, its transaction.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"141f8bb5-aab7-48df-ab13-a44d261cb6c9","uuid":"cd64584e-3ed8-4204-b503-15eac799d700","timestamp":"2026-10-27T15:58:37.868Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"\"\"\"Command-line package: `main(argv) -> int` dispatches to handlers registered by command stories.\"\"\"\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import main, register_command\nfrom cli import init_command  # noqa: F401  registers the `init` handler at import\n\n__all__ = [\"main\", \"register_command\"]\n\"\"\"Command registry and dispatch.\n\nCommand stories register a handler under a command name at import time. `main` hands the\nremaining arguments to the handler and returns the handler's exit code.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\nfrom collections.abc import Callable\n\nfrom cli import usage\n\nUSAGE_ERROR = 2\n\n_handlers: dict[str, Callable[[list[str]], int]] = {}\n\n\ndef register_command(name: str, handler: Callable[[list[str]], int]) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Map a command name to its handler; no rate from it may be written.\"\"\"\n\n\ndef parse_history(text: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Validate the whole file and return (date, currency, rate_text) for every non-N/A value.\n\n    Raises RejectedFile on the first violation found anywhere in the file.\n    \"\"\"\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(text)))\n    if not rows:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"file has no header\")\n\n    header = _drop_trailing_comma(rows[0])\n    if not header or header[0] != FIRST_HEADER_FIELD:\n        raise RejectedFile(\"header must begin with Date\")\n    currencies = header[1:]\n    for code in currencies:\n        if not _CURRENCY_PATTERN.fullmatch(code):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"malformed currency code in header: {code!r}\")\n    if len(set(currencies)) != len(currencies):\n        raise RejectedFile(\"currency code repeated in header\")\n\n    rates: list[tuple[str, str, str]] = []\n    seen_dates: set[str] = set()\n    for line_number, raw in enumerate(rows[1:], start=2):\n        fields = _drop_trailing_comma(raw)\n        if len(fields) != len(header):\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has {len(fields)} fields, expected {len(header)}\")\n\n        date_text = fields[0]\n        _check_date(date_text, line_number)\n        if date_text in seen_dates:\n            raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} repeats date {date_text}\")\n        seen_dates.add(date_text)\n\n        for code, value in zip(currencies, fields[1:]):\n            if value == NOT_AVAILABLE:\n                continue\n            _check_rate(value, line_number)\n            rates.append((date_text, code, value))\n\n    return rates\n\n\ndef _drop_trailing_comma(fields: list[str]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\"\"\"\n    if fields and fields[-1] == \"\":\n        return fields[:-1]\n    return fields\n\n\ndef _check_date(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _DATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed date: {text!r}\")\n    try:\n        datetime.date.fromisoformat(text)\n    except ValueError as error:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has an impossible date: {text!r}\") from error\n\n\ndef _check_rate(text: str, line_number: int) -> None:\n    if not _RATE_PATTERN.fullmatch(text):\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a malformed rate: {text!r}\")\n    if Decimal(text) == 0:\n        raise RejectedFile(f\"line {line_number} has a zero rate: {text!r}\")\n\"\"\"Database location: one place decides which store the application opens.\n\nResolution order: DATABASE_URL, then DATABASE_PATH, then data/app.db. The environment is read at\ncall time. Application code opens the store only through `persistence.open_database`.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\n\nfrom persistence import Database, open_database\n\nDEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH = \"data/app.db\"\nSQLITE_PREFIX = \"sqlite://\"\n\n\ndef database_path() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Return the database location from the environment, falling back to data/app.db.\"\"\"\n    url = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\", \"\")\n    if url.startswith(SQLITE_PREFIX):\n        url = url[len(SQLITE_PREFIX):]\n    if url:\n        return url\n    path = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\", \"\")\n    if path:\n        return path\n    return DEFAULT_DATABASE_PATH\n\n\ndef open_store() -> Database:\n    \"\"\"Open the store named by `database_path()` through the persistence library.\"\"\"\n    return open_database(database_path())\n\"\"\"FxRates application package.\n\nApplication modules (config, ecb, fetch, rates, history, convert, commands) are added by later\nbuild blocks. Database access goes through the shipped `persistence` package only.\n\"\"\"\n----\n#!/bin/sh\n# fxrates — application launcher. Activates .venv when present and hands the arguments to the\n# cli package. It holds no command logic; every command is dispatched by cli.main.\nROOT=\"$(cd \"$(dirname \"$0\")\" && pwd)\"\ncd \"$ROOT\"\nif [ -f \"$ROOT/.venv/bin/activate\" ]; then\n    . \"$ROOT/.venv/bin/activate\"\nfi\nexec python -m cli \"$@\"\n----\n\"\"\"Generated fixtures over the configured, already provisioned application store.\"\"\"\n\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager\nimport os\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nfrom .schema import open_database\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef committed_session():\n    \"\"\"Use normal autocommit for project tests; under the acceptance harness, its transaction.\"\"\"\n    configured = os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\") or os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_PATH\") or \"data/app.db\"\n    if not configured.startswith((\"postgres://\", \"postgresql://\")):\n        if not Path(configured.split(\"://\", 1)[-1]).is_file():\n            raise RuntimeError(\"persistence store missing; rebuild the DATABASE step\")\n    database = open_database(configured)\n    try:\n        yield database\n    finally:\n        database.close()\n\n\n@contextmanager\ndef db_session():\n    \"\"\"Share this connection with the feature; always roll back, never provision schema.\n\n    Under the acceptance harness the rollback is the harness's, at the end of the criterion, so\n    a request made after this block still sees the setup.\n    \"\"\"\n    with committed_session() as database:\n        with database.rollback_session():\n            yield database","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01ADU9zhvsJvnSognLEwobVD","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WudjP7TqDuq3cZEnDTSsH9","type":"tool_result","content":"# FEATURE: Load Validation\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | Validate a whole ECB history file before any write and return the non-N/A rates as published text. |\n| Depends On | FEATURE-InitCommand.md |\n| Provides | fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history |\n\n## Purpose\n\n`fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history(text)` checks an entire ECB history file and returns\n`(date, currency, rate_text)` for every non-N/A value, or raises `RejectedFile`. It performs no\ndatabase access. The load command (FEATURE-LoadStore.md) maps `RejectedFile` to exit 3.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. The header's first field is `Date`; every other field is a three-letter uppercase currency code.\n   The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\n2. Each row has exactly as many fields as the header, and begins with a date `YYYY-MM-DD` that is a\n   real calendar date and is not repeated within the file.\n3. A value is `N/A` (no rate, nothing returned) or matches `[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?` and is nonzero.\n4. The whole file is checked before the function returns; any violation raises `RejectedFile`, a\n   subclass of `Exception`.\n5. Rates are returned as the published text, never as a number.\n\n## Database Interface\n\n- None — persistence is owned by DATABASE.md.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC parse-valid-file ===\nIntent: A valid file yields exactly its non-N/A cells as (date, currency, text) with the published text unchanged, ignoring the trailing comma.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\n\ndef build(header, rows):\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    w.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for r in rows:\n        w.writerow(r + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\nheader = [\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\", \"ZZC\"]\nrows = [\n    [\"1900-01-03\", \"1.50\", \"N/A\", \"160.0\"],\n    [\"1900-01-02\", \"0.943\", \"2\", \"N/A\"],\n]\nresult = parse_history(build(header, rows))\nexpected = []\nfor r in rows:\n    for code, v in zip(header[1:], r[1:]):\n        if v != \"N/A\":\n            expected.append((r[0], code, v))\nassert sorted(tuple(x) for x in result) == sorted(expected)\n=== END AC parse-valid-file ===\n\n=== AC parse-only-na ===\nIntent: A file whose values are all N/A is valid and yields no rates.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\n\nbuf = io.StringIO()\nw = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\nw.writerow([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\", \"\"])\nw.writerow([\"1900-01-02\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\", \"\"])\nassert list(parse_history(buf.getvalue())) == []\n=== END AC parse-only-na ===\n\n=== AC parse-rejects-structure ===\nIntent: A wrong first header field, a malformed currency code, or a row with the wrong field count rejects the file.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history, RejectedFile\n\nassert issubclass(RejectedFile, Exception)\n\ndef build(header, rows):\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    w.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for r in rows:\n        w.writerow(r + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile:\n        return True\n    return False\n\ngood_row = [\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"]\ncases = {\n    \"bad first field\": build([\"Day\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [good_row]),\n    \"lowercase code\": build([\"Date\", \"zza\", \"ZZB\"], [good_row]),\n    \"four letter code\": build([\"Date\", \"ZZAA\", \"ZZB\"], [good_row]),\n    \"short row\": build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\"]]),\n    \"long row\": build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\", \"3.5\"]]),\n}\nfor name, text in cases.items():\n    assert rejected(text), name\n=== END AC parse-rejects-structure ===\n\n=== AC parse-rejects-dates ===\nIntent: A malformed, impossible, or repeated date rejects the whole file even when other rows are valid.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history, RejectedFile\n\ndef build(header, rows):\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    w.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for r in rows:\n        w.writerow(r + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile:\n        return True\n    return False\n\nheader = [\"Date\", \"ZZA\"]\nvalid = [\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\"]\ncases = {\n    \"unpadded\": [valid, [\"1900-1-3\", \"1.5\"]],\n    \"not a calendar date\": [valid, [\"1900-02-30\", \"1.5\"]],\n    \"month thirteen\": [valid, [\"1900-13-01\", \"1.5\"]],\n    \"repeated\": [valid, [\"1900-01-03\", \"1.6\"], [\"1900-01-03\", \"1.7\"]],\n    \"text\": [valid, [\"yesterday\", \"1.5\"]],\n}\nfor name, rows in cases.items():\n    assert rejected(build(header, rows)), name\n=== END AC parse-rejects-dates ===\n\n----\n\"\"\"Persistence access for a Drydock Target.\n\nThis file is shipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here: edit\n``DATABASE.md`` and rebuild. It is hardened and tested once, in Drydock's own suite, so every\nTarget inherits a persistence layer that has already passed rather than one re-derived from prose\non each build.\n\nThe application-facing surface is ``Database``. One attribute per declared table, one method per\ndeclared access pattern::\n\n    db = Database(dsn, SCHEMA)\n    ticket = db.tickets.get(id=7)\n    open_tickets = db.tickets.list(status=\"open\")\n\n``schema.py`` beside this file is generated from ``DATABASE.md`` and carries the tables, the\noperations, and the row types. It contains no SQL. Statements are constructed here, by the driver\nfor the engine in use, so a parameter placeholder never appears in generated code or in a caller.\n\nValues reach the database as bound parameters, never as formatted text. Identifiers cannot be\nbound in any engine, so they are taken only from the generated schema — which Drydock validated\nagainst ``^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`` before emitting it — and are quoted on the way out.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Callable, Iterable, Mapping, Sequence\nfrom dataclasses import dataclass, fields\nfrom contextlib import contextmanager, nullcontext\nimport threading\nfrom typing import Any\n\n__all__ = [\n    \"Database\",\n    \"Driver\",\n    \"Operation\",\n    \"PersistenceError\",\n    \"Schema\",\n    \"Table\",\n    \"statements\",\n    \"UnknownOperation\",\n    \"begin_acceptance_transaction\",\n    \"end_acceptance_transaction\",\n]\n\nVERBS = (\"get\", \"list\", \"create\", \"update\", \"delete\")\n#: The comparisons a declared Match term may state; anything else is refused before SQL is built.\nCOMPARISONS = (\"=\", \"<\", \"<=\", \">\", \">=\")\nDIRECTIONS = (\"asc\", \"desc\")\n\n\nclass PersistenceError(RuntimeError):\n    \"\"\"A persistence failure the caller may act on, raised in place of a driver exception.\"\"\"\n\n\nclass UnknownOperation(PersistenceError):\n    \"\"\"A verb was requested that the declaration does not grant for that table.\"\"\"\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Table:\n    \"\"\"One declared table: its columns and the column that identifies a row.\"\"\"\n\n    name: str\n    columns: tuple[str, ...]\n    primary_key: str | None = None\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Operation:\n    \"\"\"One declared access pattern, reduced to what executing it requires.\n\n    ``name`` is the method callers use and ``verb`` is its Kind, how it runs; a name that is a\n    verb runs as that verb. ``inputs`` are the parameters the caller supplies. ``match`` is the\n    equality predicate of a ``get``, ``update``, ``upsert``, or ``delete``, every field of it\n    required; a ``list`` filters on whichever inputs are supplied, and the inputs of a\n    ``create``, ``update``, or ``upsert`` outside ``match`` are the values written. ``row`` is the dataclass the operation returns, and\n    ``columns`` are its fields; an operation with no ``row`` returns a count. ``compare`` holds\n    ``(field, op, column)`` for each input compared other than by equality with its own column,\n    such as ``(\"start_date\", \">=\", \"date\")``, and ``order`` the ``(column, direction)`` sort keys\n    of a ``list``.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    identifier: str\n    table: str\n    verb: str\n    inputs: tuple[str, ...]\n    row: type | None = None\n    columns: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    match: tuple[str, ...] = ()\n    name: str = \"\"\n    compare: tuple[tuple[str, str, str], ...] = ()\n    order: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = ()\n\n    def keys(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:\n        \"\"\"The match fields compared by equality: what reads back the one row a write reached.\"\"\"\n        compared = {field for field, op, _ in self.compare if op != \"=\"}\n        return tuple(name for name in self.match if name not in compared)\n\n\n@dataclass(frozen=True)\nclass Schema:\n    \"\"\"The generated declaration: every table and every operation reaching one.\"\"\"\n\n    tables: tuple[Table, ...]\n    operations: tuple[Operation, ...]\n\n    def by_table(self) -> dict[str, tuple[Operation, ...]]:\n        grouped: dict[str, list[Operation]] = {table.name: [] for table in self.tables}\n        for operation in self.operations:\n            grouped.setdefault(operation.table, []).append(operation)\n        return {name: tuple(items) for name, items in grouped.items()}\n\n\nclass Driver:\n    \"\"\"Statement construction shared by every engine.\n\n    Subclasses supply connection handling and the two things engines genuinely disagree about:\n    how a parameter is spelled, and how a freshly inserted row reports its key. Everything else is\n    identical SQL, so it is written once here rather than twice in the engines.\n    \"\"\"\n----\n\"\"\"SQLite engine for ``db.py``.\n\nShipped by Drydock and copied into the build unchanged. Do not edit it here.\n\nSQLite is the development and test engine. It parses the same declaration PostgreSQL does and\nignores what it does not enforce — ``VARCHAR(n)`` length in particular — so one rendered schema\nserves both engines and nothing is stripped for one of them.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sqlite3\nimport threading\nfrom pathlib import Path\nfrom typing import Any\n\ntry:\n    from .db import Driver\nexcept ImportError:  # flat layout\n    from db import Driver\n\n__all__ = [\"SqliteDriver\"]\n\n\nclass SqliteDriver(Driver):\n    \"\"\"One connection per thread, opened on first use in that thread.\n\n    A ``sqlite3.Connection`` belongs to the thread that created it and raises ``ProgrammingError``\n    when used from another, so a single connection opened during construction is valid in no web\n    request at all. This is not concurrency: queries stay sequential within a workflow, and the\n    rule only stops one connection being shared across unrelated ones.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    paramstyle = \"qmark\"\n    returning = False\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str) -> None:\n        self._path = _path_from(dsn)\n        self._local = threading.local()\n        self._pinned: sqlite3.Connection | None = None\n\n    def connect(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        if self._pinned is not None:\n            return self._pinned\n        connection = getattr(self._local, \"connection\", None)\n        if connection is None:\n            connection = self._open()\n            self._local.connection = connection\n        return connection\n\n    def pin(self) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n        # Shared across threads on purpose; ``Database`` serializes every operation on it.\n        if self._pinned is None:\n            self._pinned = self._open(check_same_thread=False)\n        return self._pinned\n\n    def identity(self) -> str:\n        return self._path if self._path == \":memory:\" else str(Path(self._path).resolve())\n\n    def _open(self, *, check_same_thread: bool = True) -> sqlite3.Connection:\n---\n\"\"\"Shared pytest fixtures for the FxRates suite.\n\nTests never open a network connection. FEATURE: Load Validation\n\n| Field | Value |\n|-------|-------|\n| Version | 20261027 V1 |\n| Description | Validate a whole ECB history file before any write and return the non-N/A rates as published text. |\n| Depends On | FEATURE-InitCommand.md |\n| Provides | fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history |\n\n## Purpose\n\n`fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history(text)` checks an entire ECB history file and returns\n`(date, currency, rate_text)` for every non-N/A value, or raises `RejectedFile`. It performs no\ndatabase access. The load command (FEATURE-LoadStore.md) maps `RejectedFile` to exit 3.\n\n## Rules\n\n1. The header's first field is `Date`; every other field is a three-letter uppercase currency code.\n   The ECB writes a trailing comma on each line; the resulting empty last field is ignored.\n2. Each row has exactly as many fields as the header, and begins with a date `YYYY-MM-DD` that is a\n   real calendar date and is not repeated within the file.\n3. A value is `N/A` (no rate, nothing returned) or matches `[0-9]+(\\.[0-9]+)?` and is nonzero.\n4. The whole file is checked before the function returns; any violation raises `RejectedFile`, a\n   subclass of `Exception`.\n5. scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\n\ndef build(header, rows):\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    w.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for r in rows:\n        w.writerow(r + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\nheader = [\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\", \"ZZC\"]\nrows = [\n    [\"1900-01-03\", \"1.50\", \"N/A\", \"160.0\"],\n    [\"1900-01-02\", \"0.943\", \"2\", \"N/A\"],\n]\nresult = parse_history(build(header, rows))\nexpected = []\nfor r in rows:\n    for code, v in zip(header[1:], r[1:]):\n        if v != \"N/A\":\n            expected.append((r[0], code, v))\nassert sorted(tuple(x) for x in result) == sorted(expected)\n=== END AC parse-valid-file ===\n\n=== AC parse-only-na ===\nIntent: A file whose values are all N/A is valid and yields no rates.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\n\nbuf = io.StringIO()\nw = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\nw.writerow([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\", \"\"])\nw.writerow([\"1900-01-02\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\", \"\"])\nassert list(parse_history(buf.getvalue())) == []\n=== END AC parse-only-na ===\n\n=== AC parse-rejects-structure ===\nIntent: A wrong first header field, a malformed currency code, or a row with the wrong field count rejects the file.\nRequires: executable=python3; scope=test\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history, RejectedFile\n\nassert issubclass(RejectedFile, Exception)\n\ndef build(header, rows):\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    w = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    w.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for r in rows:\n        w.writerow(r + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\ndef rejected(text):\n    try:\n        parse_history(text)\n    except RejectedFile:\n        return True\n    return False\n\ngood_row = [\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"]\ncases = {\n    \"bad first field\": build([\"Day\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [good_row]),\n    \"lowercase code\": build([\"Date\", \"zza\", \"ZZB\"], [good_row]),\n    \"four letter code\": build([\"Date\", \"ZZAA\", \"ZZB\"], [good_row]),\n    \"short row\": build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\"]]),\n    \"long row\": build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-01-02\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\", \"3.5\"]]),\n}\nfor name, text in cases.items():\n    assert rejected(text), name\n=== END AC parse-rejects-structure ===\n\n=== AC parse-rejects-dates ===\nIntent: A malformed, impossible, or repeated date rejects the whole file even when other rows are valid.\nRequires: executable=python3; Stored state is read back through `db.rates` rather than inferred from output.\n\n`init` removes every row, so each test runs inside one acceptance transaction: the command and the\nread-back share one connection, and the transaction rolls back at the end. The configured store is\nnever left changed.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom persistence import db as the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef test_init_removes_seeded_rates_for_a_currency(cli_runner) -> None:\n    currency = \"ZZI\"\n    date = \"1900-10-01\"\n    with db_session() as db:\n        db.rates.replace_rate(date=date, currency=currency, rate=\"1.10\")\n        assert [r.date for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)] == [date]\n\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"init\")\n\n        assert code == {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_018V6hqyiJsEKtc3g5CVxxoE","type":"tool_result","content":"        if operation is None:\n            granted = \", \".join(sorted(self._operations)) or \"none\"\n            raise UnknownOperation(\n                f\"{self._table.name} declares no {name!r} operation. Declared: {granted}. \"\n                \"Add an access pattern to DATABASE.md rather than reaching around this class.\"\n            )\n        return lambda **arguments: self._database.run(operation, arguments)\n\n\nclass _AcceptanceTransaction:\n    \"\"\"One transaction per store, shared by every ``Database`` this process opens; never committed.\n\n    The acceptance harness begins it before a criterion runs and rolls it back when the criterion\n    ends. The criterion's fixture, the application behind an in-process HTTP client, and an\n    in-process command all join it, so setup, behavior and readback see one another's writes and\n    none of them persists. A crash loses nothing: an engine discards an uncommitted transaction.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self) -> None:\n        self.lock = threading.RLock()\n        self._drivers: dict[str, Driver] = {}\n\n    def join(self, driver: Driver) -> Driver:\n        with self.lock:\n            shared = self._drivers.get(driver.identity())\n            if shared is None:\n                cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n                finally:\n                    cursor.close()\n                shared = self._drivers[driver.identity()] = driver\n            return shared\n\n    def rollback(self) -> None:\n        failures = []\n        with self.lock:\n            for identity, driver in self._drivers.items():\n                try:\n                    cursor = driver.pin().cursor()\n                    try:\n                        cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                    finally:\n                        cursor.close()\n                except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - every store is still closed\n                    failures.append(f\"{identity}: {exc}\")\n                finally:\n                    driver.close()\n            self._drivers.clear()\n        if failures:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"acceptance rollback failed: \" + \"; \".join(failures))\n\n\n_harness: _AcceptanceTransaction | None = None\n\n\ndef begin_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Join every store this process opens from now on to one transaction the harness owns.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    if _harness is None:\n        _harness = _AcceptanceTransaction()\n\n\ndef end_acceptance_transaction() -> None:\n    \"\"\"Roll back the harness's transaction on every store it joined.\"\"\"\n    global _harness\n    harness, _harness = _harness, None\n    if harness is not None:\n        harness.rollback()\n\n\nclass Database:\n    \"\"\"One store, presented to callers as declared tables with declared methods.\n\n    Callers construct one instance, share it freely, and call methods synchronously. Connection\n    handling is internal and may change without affecting any caller.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, dsn: str, schema: Schema, *, driver: Driver | None = None) -> None:\n        self._rollback_owner = None\n        self._schema = schema\n        driver = driver if driver is not None else open_driver(dsn)\n        self._harness = _harness\n        self._driver = self._harness.join(driver) if self._harness is not None else driver\n        grouped = schema.by_table()\n        for table in schema.tables:\n            setattr(self, table.name, TableAccess(table, grouped.get(table.name, ()), self))\n\n    @property\n    def driver(self) -> Driver:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction\")\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"driver access is forbidden inside a rollback session\")\n        return self._driver\n\n    def close(self) -> None:\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            return  # the acceptance harness owns the shared connection\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"the rollback session owns connection lifetime\")\n        self._driver.close()\n\n    @contextmanager\n    def rollback_session(self):\n        \"\"\"Use this connection for setup, behavior and assertions; always roll back.\n\n        Normal calls remain autocommitted. No schema creation, nested transaction,\n        driver escape, or cross-thread operation is allowed in this scope. Under the acceptance\n        harness the scope is the harness's transaction, rolled back when the criterion ends, so\n        leaving it rolls nothing back.\n        \"\"\"\n        if self._harness is not None:\n            yield self\n            return\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"nested rollback session\")\n        connection = self._driver.connect()\n        cursor = connection.cursor()\n        try:\n            cursor.execute(\"BEGIN\")\n            self._rollback_owner = threading.get_ident()\n            try:\n                yield self\n            finally:\n                try:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK\")\n                except Exception as exc:\n                    raise PersistenceError(f\"acceptance rollback failed: {exc}\") from exc\n                finally:\n                    self._rollback_owner = None\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n            self._driver.close()\n\n    def __enter__(self) -> Database:\n        return self\n\n    def __exit__(self, *_: object) -> None:\n        self.close()\n\n    def execute_script(self, sql: str) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Apply generated DDL. The schema is built once, at the DATABASE build step.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None:\n            raise PersistenceError(\"schema and transaction SQL are forbidden in rollback sessions\")\n        cursor = self._open(\"schema\")\n        try:\n            for statement in statements(self._driver.prepare_schema(sql)):\n                cursor.execute(statement)\n        finally:\n            cursor.close()\n\n    def run(self, operation: Operation, arguments: Mapping[str, Any]) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Execute one declared operation with bound parameters.\"\"\"\n        unknown = sorted(set(arguments) - set(operation.inputs))\n        if unknown:\n            raise PersistenceError(\n                f\"{operation.identifier} does not accept {', '.join(unknown)}. Declared inputs: \"\n                f\"{', '.join(operation.inputs) or 'none'}.\"\n            )\n        if operation not in self._schema.operations:\n            raise UnknownOperation(f\"{operation.identifier} is not a declared operation\")\n        missing = [name for name in self._match(operation) if name not in arguments]\n        if missing:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires {', '.join(missing)}\")\n        if operation.verb == \"delete\" and not arguments:\n            raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} requires a delete predicate\")\n        names = [name for name in operation.inputs if name in arguments]\n        values = [arguments[name] for name in names]\n        # The harness's one connection serves the criterion and the application's request\n        # threads alike, so an operation holds it for its whole statement and savepoint.\n        with self._harness.lock if self._harness is not None else nullcontext():\n            scoped = self._rollback_owner is not None or self._harness is not None\n            cursor = self._open(operation.identifier)\n            try:\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                result = self._dispatch(operation, cursor, names, values)\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                return result\n            except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - translated at the boundary on purpose\n                if scoped:\n                    cursor.execute(\"ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                    cursor.execute(\"RELEASE SAVEPOINT drydock_operation\")\n                raise PersistenceError(f\"{operation.identifier} failed: {exc}\") from exc\n            finally:\n                cursor.close()\n\n    def _open(self, action: str) -> Any:\n        \"\"\"Return a cursor, translating a refused or failed connection.\"\"\"\n        if self._rollback_owner not in (None, threading.get_ident()):\n            raise PersistenceError(\"rollback session requires its owning thread and connection\")\n        try:\n            return self._driver.connect().cursor()\n        except PersistenceError:\n            raise\n        except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 - {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT23LDWu5gWMwK1egGjL","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01TVHVTrrXLP6jdo6RToU8GV","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/cli/load_command.py","content":"\"\"\"The `load` command: validate an ECB history file, store its rates, report the counts.\n\n`parse_history` checks the whole file before the first write, so a rejected file exits 3 and stores\nnothing. Each rate is then written through the declared `rates.replace_rate` operation, which\nreplaces a rate already stored for the same date and currency, so loading a file twice leaves the\ndatabase unchanged.\n\nThe persistence library exposes no transaction operation, so each replace commits on its own. The\nvalidation above is what keeps a rejected file from changing anything; a store failure part way\nthrough a valid file is not rolled back.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport sys\n\nfrom cli.dispatcher import register_command\nfrom fxrates_app.config import open_store\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import RejectedFile, parse_history\n\nREJECTED = 3\nHELP_FLAG = \"--help\"\n\n\ndef load(rest: list[str]) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Load the file named in `rest[0]` and return the exit code. {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT24Fjv1Hbcj1oUBw7dA","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01G3bJjFZiseTxvfsZ5nyeTk","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/mnt/c/Users/barlo/projects/drydock/uat/FxRates/runs/20261027.152427/build/FxRates/tests/test_load.py","content":"\"\"\"The `load` command: validates a file, stores its rates as text, reports the dates and rates counts.\n\nEach test runs the command in-process through `cli_runner` and reads the stored state back through\n`db.rates`. Every test shares one acceptance transaction with the command, which rolls back at the\nend, so the configured store is never left changed. Test currencies use the ZZ prefix so they never\ncollide with rates already in a store.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef build(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write(tmp_path: Path, name: str, text: str) -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_exits_zero_and_reports_dates_and_rates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"1.5\", \"2\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"0.9\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"2,3\"]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_stores_each_rate_as_published_text(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\", \"160.0\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\")]\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZB\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"160.0\")]\n\n\ndef test_all_na_date_is_not_counted_as_a_date(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(\n        tmp_path,\n        \"in.csv\",\n        build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-03\", \"1.5\", \"N/A\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]),\n    )\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"1,1\"]\n\n\ndef test_file_of_only_na_reports_zero_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"na.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZH\", \"ZZI\"], [[\"1900-08-05\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n\n        code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"0,0\"]\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=\"1900-08-05\") == []\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == before\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_reports_the_same_counts(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"], [\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    first = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n    second = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert first[0] == second[0] == 0\n    assert first[1] == second[1]\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_leaves_stored_rates_unchanged(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"], [\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n        once = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == once\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\"), Test currencies use the ZZ prefix so they never\ncollide with rates already in a store.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef build(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write(tmp_path: Path, name: str, text: str) -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_exits_zero_and_reports_dates_and_rates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"1.5\", \"2\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"0.9\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"2,3\"]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_stores_each_rate_as_published_text(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\", \"160.0\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\")]\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZB\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"160.0\")]\n\n\ndef test_all_na_date_is_not_counted_as_a_date(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(\n        tmp_path,\n        \"in.csv\",\n        build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-03\", \"1.5\", \"N/A\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]),\n    )\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"1,1\"]\n\n\ndef test_file_of_only_na_reports_zero_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"na.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZH\", \"ZZI\"], [[\"1900-08-05\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n\n        code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"0,0\"]\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=\"1900-08-05\") == []\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == before\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_reports_the_same_counts(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\",  assert first[0] == second[0] == 0\n    assert first[1] == second[1]\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_leaves_stored_rates_unchanged(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, once = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == once\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\"), (\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\")]\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZB\") == [(\"1900-08-12\", \"2.5\")]\n\n\ndef test_later_file_replaces_stored_rate_and_keeps_other_dates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef build(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write(tmp_path: Path, name: str, text: str) -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_exits_zero_and_reports_dates_and_rates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"1.5\", \"2\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"0.9\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"2,3\"]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_stores_each_rate_as_published_text(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", path = write(\n        tmp_path,\n        \"in.csv\",\n        build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-03\", \"1.5\", \"N/A\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]),\n    )\n\n    code, out, _ Every test shares one acceptance transaction with the command, which rolls back at the\nend, so the configured store is never left changed. Test currencies use the ZZ prefix so they never\ncollide with rates already in a store.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nfrom collections.abc import Iterator\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nimport pytest\n\nfrom fxrates_app.ecb import parse_history\nfrom persistence import db as persistence_db\nfrom persistence.testing import db_session\n\n\n@pytest.fixture(autouse=True)\ndef rolled_back_transaction() -> Iterator[None]:\n    \"\"\"Share one connection between the command and the test, then roll everything back.\"\"\"\n    persistence_db.begin_acceptance_transaction()\n    try:\n        yield\n    finally:\n        persistence_db.end_acceptance_transaction()\n\n\ndef build(header: list[str], rows: list[list[str]]) -> str:\n    \"\"\"Write a file the way the ECB does: every line ends with a trailing comma.\"\"\"\n    buf = io.StringIO()\n    writer = csv.writer(buf, lineterminator=\"\\n\")\n    writer.writerow(header + [\"\"])\n    for row in rows:\n        writer.writerow(row + [\"\"])\n    return buf.getvalue()\n\n\ndef write(tmp_path: Path, name: str, text: str) -> str:\n    path = tmp_path / name\n    path.write_text(text, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    return str(path)\n\n\ndef stored(db, currency: str) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n    return [(r.date, r.rate) for r in db.rates.list_currency_history(currency=currency)]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_exits_zero_and_reports_dates_and_rates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"1.5\", \"2\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"0.9\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"2,3\"]\n\n\ndef test_valid_file_stores_each_rate_as_published_text(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\", \"160.0\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        code, _, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"0.943\")]\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZB\") == [(\"1900-08-02\", \"160.0\")]\n\n\ndef test_all_na_date_is_not_counted_as_a_date(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(\n        tmp_path,\n        \"in.csv\",\n        build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-03\", \"1.5\", \"N/A\"], [\"1900-08-01\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]),\n    )\n\n    code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert code == 0\n    assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"1,1\"]\n\n\ndef test_file_of_only_na_reports_zero_and_stores_nothing(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"na.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZH\", \"ZZI\"], [[\"1900-08-05\", \"N/A\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n\n        code, out, _ = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert code == 0\n        assert out.splitlines() == [\"dates,rates\", \"0,0\"]\n        assert db.rates.list_for_date(date=\"1900-08-05\") == []\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == before\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_reports_the_same_counts(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"], [\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    first = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n    second = cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n    assert first[0] == second[0] == 0\n    assert first[1] == second[1]\n\n\ndef test_loading_same_file_twice_leaves_stored_rates_unchanged(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n    path = write(tmp_path, \"in.csv\", build([\"Date\", \"ZZA\", \"ZZB\"], [[\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\", \"2.5\"], [\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\", \"N/A\"]]))\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n        once = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n        cli_runner(\"load\", path)\n\n        assert db.rates.list_all_keys() == once\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZA\") == [(\"1900-08-11\", \"1.25\"), (\"1900-08-12\", \"1.5\")]\n        assert stored(db, \"ZZB\") == [(\"1900-08-12\", \"2.5\")]\n\n\ndef test_later_file_replaces_stored_rate_and_keeps_other_dates(cli_runner, tmp_path) -> None:\n build([\"Date\", \"ZZB\", \"\"], [[\"1900-08-31\", \"1.5\", \"\"], [\"1900-08-30\", \"1.0x\", \"\"]]),\n    )\n\n    with db_session() as db:\n        before = db.rates.list_all_keys()\n\n {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CgT2BaQGV9YEinSBg7wZK","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"`fxrates load` is implemented and the declared gate passes. One requirement is not met: the load is not a single transaction.\n\n**What's not met:** FEATURE-LoadStore asks for all rates to be stored in one transaction. The persistence library has no transaction operation, and driver access is blocked inside the acceptance transaction, so `cli/` cannot open one without reaching around the library. Each `rates.replace_rate` commits on its own. The validation runs before the first write, so a rejected file still stores nothing. A database error part way through a valid file would leave a partial load. Fixing this needs a transaction operation in DATABASE.md or the shipped persistence layer, which are Drydock-owned.\n\nRESULT: SUCCESS\n\nFILES CHANGED:\n- cli/load_command.py\n- cli/__init__.py\n- tests/test_load.py\n\nSUMMARY:\n- `cli/load_command.py` registers the `load` handler. It reads the file, runs `fxrates_app.ecb.parse_history` over the whole file, and returns exit 3 with one stderr line and empty stdout on `RejectedFile`. On success it writes each rate through `db.rates.replace_rate` and prints `dates,rates` then `<dates>,<rates>`.\n- `cli/__init__.py` imports the new module, the same way `init` is registered.\n- `tests/test_load.py` has 15 tests. They cover counts, all-N/A dates, text rate storage, reload idempotence, replacement without adding rows, rejected files storing nothing, and the supplied good and bad ECB files. Reads go back through `db.rates`, and each test runs in the rolled-back acceptance transaction.\n\nChecks run:\n- `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_load.py`: 15 passed. One of my tests first failed because I wrote a bad header in it. I fixed the test, not the command.\n- `sh bin/test.sh`: exit 0, 149 passed.\n- End-to-end on a temp copy of the store (`DATABASE_PATH`): the January file gives `22,176` twice; the bad file gives exit 3 with `error: line 3 has a malformed rate: '1.0x'`; the Feb 3–4 file gives `2,16`; `load` with no argument gives exit 2. The shipped `data/app.db` was not touched.\n- I did not run the acceptance assertions directly. Drydock runs them after this step.\n\nChoices I made:\n- `load --help` returns 0 with no output and does not read a file, matching how `init` treats its arguments. The spec does not cover it.\n- A missing or unreadable file raises an `OSError` and is not caught. That belongs to FEATURE-LoadUnreadable, which is not in this block.\n\n```blueprint-decisions\n[{\"spec\":\"FEATURE-LoadStore.md\",\"severity\":\"Material\",\"subject\":\"Single transaction for the load\",\"decision\":\"The spec asks for all upserts in one transaction. The persistence library exposes no transaction operation, and driver access is forbidden inside the acceptance transaction, so cli/ cannot open one without bypassing the library. I wrote each rate through rates.replace_rate, which autocommits per row. Validation still runs over the whole file before the first write, so rejected files store nothing, but a database failure mid-load is not rolled back. Should a transaction operation be added to DATABASE.md, or is per-row commit acceptable?\"},{\"spec\":\"FEATURE-LoadStore.md\",\"severity\":\"Low\",\"subject\":\"load --help handling\",\"decision\":\"load --help returns exit 0 with no output and does not read a file, matching init. The spec does not define it. Confirm or change on replan.\"}]\n```\n\nFAILURE_SUMMARY is not needed because the result is SUCCESS, with the atomicity gap reported above."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":855,"cache_read_input_tokens":64051,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":855},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"global","speed":"standard"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"141f8bb5-aab7-48df-ab13-a44d261cb6c9","uuid":"75b4f396-e401-489a-b1a9-47cdb7fbe866","timestamp":"2026-10-27T16:00:59.071Z","request_id":"req_011CgT2Ba7uXVVsrugDs4BiQ"}
